ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Viewed from top to bottom, there is an induced current in the clockwise direction in the elastic circular ring

Now the elastic circular ring is uniformly expanded outward. Viewed from top to bottom, what is the direction of the induced current in the elastic circular ring?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a vertically placed bar magnet, with the upper end of the magnet marked S and the lower end marked N; a closed metal elastic circular ring is horizontally sleeved near the center of the magnet, and the axis of the circular ring coincides with the center line of the bar magnet. The problem requires judging the direction of the induced current in the circular ring when the circular ring is uniformly expanded outward, viewed from top to bottom. Reasoning: The magnetic field lines outside the magnet start from the N pole and return to the S pole. Since in the figure the lower end is N and the upper end is S, near the outside of the center of the magnet and the region where the circular ring is located, the direction of the external magnetic field passing through the plane of the circular ring is generally upward. When the circular ring is uniformly expanded outward, the area enclosed by the circular ring increases, and therefore the upward magnetic flux passing through the circular ring increases. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current should hinder this increase in upward magnetic flux, so the induced current should produce a downward magnetic field. Then using the right-hand screw rule to judge: viewed from top to bottom, if the circular current produces a downward magnetic field, then the current direction is clockwise. Therefore the direction of the induced current in the elastic circular ring is clockwise.
